hedges.reason: The strikes on this ladder run from $90 to $200, which suggests crude is already high in an ongoing Iran and Gulf crisis. The most likely route to a Fed reversal is energy-driven inflation. If WTI stays at or above the low rungs through late June, the headline CPI and inflation-expectations pressure that could push the committee to hike in July, September or October is already building.

A formal US naval blockade of Iran or of Hormuz traffic is the clearest supply shock available in this list. It would push oil and gasoline sharply higher and pass into CPI and inflation expectations over the months running up to the September and October meetings. That is exactly the world where the NO-hike basket fails. The mild tier is the widest window, running to Dec 31, and it covers escalation before the October meeting.

If no further senior-level US-Iran round takes place by Sept 30, the June 22 roadmap has broken down. That points to renewed escalation and a persistent oil risk premium, which keep the energy inflation impulse alive into the fall meetings, the states where a hike becomes possible.

claims.reason: A hike at the July 28-29 meeting would reverse the easing cycle with almost no warning. That would take an inflation shock already visible before the meeting, and in this world energy is the only plausible trigger. Crude would therefore have to be at elevated levels during June.

A September hike needs the June-August CPI prints to show a re-acceleration. Given the lag from crude to gasoline to headline CPI, that shock has to be in oil prices by June. So a September hike implies crude was high in June.
